root_cause.text: In the Tegra194 PCIe endpoint path, `pex_ep_event_pex_rst_deassert()` invoked `pci_epc_deinit_notify()`/`dw_pcie_ep_cleanup()` before `reset_control_deassert(pcie->core_rst)` powered on the controller core, causing DBI accesses in the cleanup path to hit inaccessible hardware and trigger a CBB timeout.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE description and patch show the timeout call chain leading from `pci_epc_deinit_notify()` to `dw_pcie_dbi_ro_wr_en()` accessing DBI register `0x8bc (PCIE_MISC_CONTROL_1_OFF)`, and the diff fixes it by moving `pci_epc_deinit_notify(pcie->pci.ep.epc)` and `dw_pcie_ep_cleanup(&pcie->pci.ep)` to after `reset_control_deassert(pcie->core_rst)`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Avoid perform endpoint cleanup during PEX reset deassert handling while preserving interrupt status clearing.
intent_record.what: Removed the cleanup sequence in pex_ep_event_pex_rst_deassert() that called pci_epc_deinit_notify(pcie->pci.ep.epc) and dw_pcie_ep_cleanup(&pcie->pci.ep) after the refclk-related comment, leaving the subsequent interrupt status clearing code in place.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the function no longer performs endpoint controller deinitialization and endpoint cleanup during PEX reset deassert handling, so those resources and callbacks are not torn down at that point; the stale interrupt status clearing still occurs as before.

intent_record.intent_summary: Move endpoint deinitialization and cleanup to the post-reset path so cleanup that depends on refclk and core reset deassertion runs correctly.
intent_record.what: Two calls were inserted immediately after `reset_control_deassert(pcie->core_rst)`: a comment and a call to `pci_epc_deinit_notify(pcie->pci.ep.epc)`, followed by a call to `dw_pcie_ep_cleanup(&pcie->pci.ep)`.
intent_record.how: After the core reset is deasserted, the code now explicitly notifies the endpoint controller of deinitialization and performs endpoint cleanup at a point where the refclk and core reset are available. This ensures cleanup actions that depend on the hardware being out of reset can run correctly, rather than being deferred or skipped.

grouping_result.intent: Move endpoint deinitialization and cleanup to the post-reset path so cleanup that depends on refclk and core reset deassertion runs correctly.

consistency_review.core_intent: Defer endpoint cleanup/deinitialization until after reset deassertion so cleanup runs in the correct post-reset state while preserving necessary status handling.

relevance_review.reason: The changes directly match the root cause: they defer endpoint deinitialization/cleanup until after reset deassertion, avoiding DBI accesses while the controller core is still inaccessible and preventing the CBB timeout.

candidates.rationale: The bug occurs because endpoint cleanup/deinitialization was performed before the controller core was brought out of reset. This line marks the point where the core is actually deasserted; having cleanup happen before this statement means DBI accesses in the cleanup path can hit inaccessible hardware and time out.

This is one of the cleanup calls executed too early in the pre-fix flow. It triggers endpoint deinitialization before the PCIe core has been powered back on, which can lead to DBI accesses against inaccessible hardware.

This cleanup routine was invoked before reset deassertion in the vulnerable code path. Because it can access DBI/register state, running it while the core is still in reset is the direct cause of the timeout.

vuln_statements.explanation: This endpoint deinitialization was executed in the PEX reset deassert handler before the controller core was brought out of reset, causing cleanup code to touch DBI registers while hardware was still inaccessible.
This cleanup routine ran too early in the vulnerable flow, before reset_control_deassert(pcie->core_rst);, which could trigger DBI accesses against a powered-off core and lead to the timeout.
